attributes.name: [GCP Compute Engine OTel] Average disk I/O latency 99.5% rolling 30 days
attributes.description: This SLO tracks the I/O latency of each Compute Engine persistent disk and Hyperdisk volume, as observed by the hypervisor through the Google Cloud Monitoring receiver. A 5-minute timeslice is good when the average of compute.googleapis.com/instance/disk/average_io_latency for the disk stays below 50 ms (50000 microseconds). The objective is that 99.5% of 5-minute timeslices are good over a rolling 30-day period. Sustained high average I/O latency stalls databases, queues and other I/O-bound workloads running on the VM. It is caused either by saturation (IOPS or throughput approaching the provisioned or size-based ceiling, visible as rising average_io_queue_depth) or by Compute Engine infrastructure degradation (instance/disk/performance_status = Severely Degraded). The 50 ms threshold is deliberately set for the slowest standard disk type (pd-standard, HDD-backed); for fleets of SSD-backed disks (pd-balanced, pd-ssd, Hyperdisk) consider cloning this SLO with a storage_type filter and a tighter threshold. The metric does not carry instance_name, so instances are identified by instance_id and the disk by device_name.
